# 1 Maccabees Chapter 12 — The EMET Bible (Literal)

**Translator:** EMET | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus, 1 Maccabees 12 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-DC/1MA_012_page_001.jpg

---

**1** And Jonathan saw that the time was favorable for him, and he chose men and sent them to Rome to confirm and renew the friendship with them.

**2** And he sent letters also to the Spartans and to other places, for the same purpose.

**3** And they went to Rome and entered the senate and said: "Jonathan the high priest and the Jewish nation have sent us to renew the friendship and the alliance with you, as it was before."

**4** And they gave them letters to the local authorities in each place, that they should give them safe conduct to the land of Judah.

**5** And this is the copy of the letters that Jonathan wrote to the Spartans:

**6** "Jonathan the high priest and the council of elders of the nation and the priests and the rest of the Jewish people to their brothers the Spartans, greetings.

**7** Already formerly letters were sent to Onias the high priest from Arius who was reigning among you, that you are our brothers, as the copy that is written below shows.

**8** And Onias welcomed the envoy with honor and received the letters, which contained a clear declaration concerning alliance and friendship.

**9** Therefore, even though we do not need these things, having for our encouragement the holy books that are in our hands,

**10** we venture to send to renew the brotherhood and friendship with you, lest we become estranged from you, for it is a long time since you sent to us.

**11** We therefore at all times without ceasing at every feast and on other appointed days make mention of you before the sacrifices and in the prayers, as it is right and proper to be mindful of brothers.

**12** And we rejoice in your glory.

**13** But as for us, many tribulations and wars have surrounded us, and the kings who are round about us have made war on us.

**14** We did not want to trouble you or our other allies and friends with these wars,

**15** for we have the help from heaven that aids us, and we have been delivered from our enemies, and our enemies have been humbled.

**16** We therefore chose Numenius son of Antiochus and Antipater son of Jason and sent them to the Romans to renew the former friendship and alliance with them.

**17** We instructed them to go also to you and greet you and deliver to you our letter concerning the renewal of our brotherhood.

**18** And now please send us your reply on this."

**19** And this is the copy of the letter that they had sent to Onias:

**20** "Arius king of the Spartans to Onias the great priest, greetings.

**21** It has been found in a writing concerning the Spartans and the Jews, that they are brothers and are of the family of Abraham.

**22** And now since we have learned this, please write to us concerning your welfare.

**23** We also write to you: your cattle and your goods are ours, and ours are yours. We therefore command that they shall report this to you."

**24** And Jonathan heard that the generals of Demetrius had returned to fight against him with a greater force than before.

**25** And he set out from Jerusalem and met them in the territory of Hamath, for he gave them no opportunity to set foot in his territory.

**26** And he sent spies into their camp, and they returned and reported to him that they were making preparations to come upon them by night.

**27** And when the sun went down, Jonathan commanded his men to be on the watch and to have their weapons at hand and to be ready for battle all night, and he posted outposts around the camp.

**28** And the enemies heard that Jonathan was ready with his men for battle, and they were afraid and were troubled in their hearts, and they kindled fires in their camp and went away.

**29** But Jonathan and his men did not know it until morning, for they saw the fires burning.

**30** And Jonathan pursued them, but he did not overtake them, for they had crossed the Jordan.

**31** And Jonathan turned aside to the Arabs who are called Zabadeans and struck them and took their spoils.

**32** And he broke camp and came to Damascus and traveled through all that country.

**33** And Simon went out and traveled as far as Ashkelon and the nearby fortresses; and he turned aside to Joppa and took possession of it,

**34** for he had heard that they intended to hand it over to the men of Demetrius; and he set a garrison there to guard it.

**35** And Jonathan returned and assembled the council of elders of the people, and he took counsel with them to build strongholds in Judea

**36** and to heighten the walls of Jerusalem and to raise a great mound between the citadel and the city to separate it from the city and make it isolated, so that they might not buy and sell.

**37** And they gathered together to build up the city, for part of the wall on the east side had fallen, and he repaired the one called Chaphenatha.

**38** And Simon built Adida in the lowland and made it strong, and set up gates with bars.

**39** Now Trypho sought to become king over Asia and to put on the crown and to stretch out his hand against Antiochus the king.

**40** And he was afraid that Jonathan would not allow him and that he would fight against him, and he sought to seize and kill him; and he arose and came to Beth-shan.

**41** And Jonathan went out to meet him with forty thousand chosen men of war and came to Beth-shan.

**42** And Trypho saw that he came with a great army, and he feared to stretch out his hand against him.

**43** And he received him with honor and commended him to all his friends and gave him gifts and commanded his armies to be obedient to him as to himself.

**44** And he said to Jonathan: "Why have you wearied all this people when we have no war?

**45** Now therefore send them back to their homes, and choose for yourself a few men who shall be with you, and come with me to Ptolemais, and I will deliver it to you and all the remaining strongholds and the remaining troops and all the officials, and I will turn and go back; for this is why I came."

**46** And Jonathan trusted him and did as he said, and dismissed his troops, and they went away into the land of Judah.

**47** And he kept with himself three thousand men, of whom he left two thousand in Galilee, and one thousand went with him.

**48** But as Jonathan entered Ptolemais, the men of Ptolemais shut the gates and seized him, and all those who had come with him they killed with the sword.

**49** And Trypho sent cavalry and foot soldiers into Galilee and the Great Plain to destroy all Jonathan's men.

**50** But they were informed that Jonathan had been seized and had perished, and those with him; and they encouraged each other and went in close formation, ready for war.

**51** And those who were pursuing them saw that they were ready to fight for their lives and turned back.

**52** And they all came safely into the land of Judah and they mourned Jonathan and those with him, and were greatly afraid; and all Israel made great lamentation.

**53** And all the nations around them sought to destroy them utterly, for they said: "They have no leader or helper; now therefore let us fight against them and destroy the memory of them from among men."
